styles.label: History
styles.blurb: The Freedom Trail, Old North Church and the harbour's past.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Chowder, lobster rolls and the North End's Italian lanes.

styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Museums, Fenway Park and student-city energy.

stays.why: Walk to the Freedom Trail, Faneuil Hall and the aquarium. Best base for a first visit.
Pretty streets, shopping on Newbury Street and easy T rides to the centre.
Quiet brick lanes next to Boston Common and the State House; small inns and guesthouses.
New waterfront hotels, harbour views and the ICA museum; 15–20 minutes' walk to downtown.

food: Try a lobster roll and New England clam chowder; prices vary a lot, so compare menus before you sit down.
Walk the North End for Italian pastries and pasta; it is busy at weekends, so go early or on a weekday.
Faneuil Hall and Quincy Market have many food stalls — handy for groups with different tastes.
For cheap eats, look around Chinatown and the student areas near universities.
Book popular dinner spots ahead, especially in summer and on game nights near Fenway Park.
more_time: Swap a city day for Cambridge: walk or take the Red Line to Harvard Square and the MIT area.
Take a harbour ferry or water taxi for a cheap view of the skyline and the waterfront.
Add a day trip by train to Salem or Providence; check timetables on the day.

recommend.why: Two nights cover the Freedom Trail, the North End and a museum; add a night for Cambridge or a harbour day.

month_notes: Coldest month: highs near 3°C, lows near -5°C. Pack a warm coat, hat and gloves.
Still deep winter: highs near 4°C, lows near -6°C. Snow is possible; wear boots with grip.
Cool and changeable: highs near 8°C, lows near -2°C, with about 12 wet days.
Spring arrives: highs near 13°C, lows near 4°C. A light jacket and layers work well.
Pleasant: highs near 20°C, lows near 10°C. Good walking weather; keep a rain layer.
Warm and lively: highs near 25°C, lows near 15°C. Book hotels early.
Hot and humid: highs near 28°C, lows near 19°C. Plan indoor breaks in the afternoon.
Similar to July: highs near 28°C, lows near 18°C. Carry water on long walks.
Warm and comfortable: highs near 23°C, lows near 15°C. A great month for the trail.
Crisp autumn: highs near 17°C, lows near 9°C. Bring a sweater for evenings.
Cooler: highs near 11°C, lows near 2°C, with fewer wet days (about 8).
Cold again: highs near 6°C, lows near -2°C. Expect about 11 wet days; pack warm layers.

climate_guide.summary: Four clear seasons: cold, sometimes snowy winters and warm, humid summers. Spring and autumn are the easiest months for walking.

items.title: Best time: May, June, September and October
items.text: Highs around 17–25°C and lows around 9–15°C. Comfortable for the Freedom Trail and the waterfront.

items.title: Winter is cold (December to February)
items.text: Highs near 3–6°C and lows near -6 to -2°C. Snow and ice are possible; wear warm, waterproof boots.

items.title: Summer is warm and humid (July and August)
items.text: Highs near 28°C with lows near 18–19°C. Take indoor breaks and carry water.

items.title: Rain in every month
items.text: About 8–12 wet days a month. A small umbrella or rain jacket is worth packing year-round.

items.title: Autumn cools quickly
items.text: October highs near 17°C drop to about 11°C in November. Bring layers for evenings.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Comfortable walking shoes, layers, and a rain layer. Add a warm coat, hat and gloves from December to March.

transit.best: Walk central Boston and use the T for longer hops; the Silver Line is free from the airport.

modes.text: The T subway has four colour-coded lines; the Blue Line links the airport area to downtown. Use a CharlieCard and tap in.
Buses use the same CharlieCard. The Silver Line bus runs free from Logan to South Station and connects to the Red Line.
Taxis are mostly white and cost $25–50 from Logan to downtown. Uber and Lyft pick up and drop off at Logan; check the current pickup zone.
Not needed for central Boston, which is compact and walkable. Consider one only for trips outside the city.
Central Boston is compact and walkable. Wear comfortable shoes for the Freedom Trail.
Ferries serve the harbour and are a good way to see the waterfront. Check times on the day.
